title: Process
description: processes/<id>.json (1.2.7): a process as an event log over the ontology. `events` lists the tables the events come from and the objects each event is about; `clean` tidies them. A build (after save_process, and after each refresh of a table it reads) writes model table pm_<id>_events, one row per event, and one pm_<id>_<type> per object type, the events of each object of that type in order; each row of it also carries its case's own figures (variant_id, cycle_seconds) and two flags (first_visit, first_pair), so these names are the build's own. An event on several objects is one row in pm_<id>_events and one per object in a type's table: an event's own figures (how many events, an amount, working time) are counted from pm_<id>_events; a type's table counts per object of that type. A type's table is filtered by its object's row-level security rules; pm_<id>_events holds every event, so restricted readers get no rows of it once a rule filters something it is built from. While a column-level security rule names a table the process reads (a source, a bridge table, an object type's table) or one of its own tables, restricted readers get no rows of any of its tables: what a build makes of a column (an event's id, a copy under another name, the order of the rows) could show what the rule hides. Known limit: where a restricted reader sees a type's objects only through a link that row-level security follows (`rls: follow`), that type's table shows them no rows at all (it fails closed) instead of their objects' events. Times: an instant (a TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE column) is read as wall-clock time in the project's time zone, and a `clean.where` value for one is such a time, without an offset; a change of the project's time zone builds the event log again; after a change of the tenant's default zone, or a move of the project to another tenant, save the process again. `reference.end` decides when a case has ended in process_performance; the rest of `reference`, `sla` and `refresh_minutes` are kept in the file and checked for their shape only: nothing reads them yet. Builds live in the registry, not in Git.

id.description: Equals the file name; part of the generated tables' names (pm_<id>_events, pm_<id>_<type>)

case.description: The object type a view starts from; one of the types under `objects`

events.description: Where the events come from. A source is an event table (`activity` and `start`, one event per row) or a table with several timestamp columns (`stamps`, one event per row and filled timestamp)

id.description: The column that identifies an event (needed for `through`); without it events are numbered by their row

activity.description: The text column naming what happened

start.description: The DATE or TIMESTAMP column saying when it happened (or began); a row without it is dropped

end.description: The DATE or TIMESTAMP column saying when it ended: gives the event its duration

attributes.description: Other columns kept on the event (who did it, an amount)

stamps.description: Activity name to the DATE or TIMESTAMP column holding when it happened: each row gives one event per filled column; events of one row at the same time keep the order of the table's columns

objects.description: The objects an event is about. An event with none is dropped

type.description: An object type ID of model/ontology.json

columns.description: The columns holding the object's key, in key order: of the source table (at most one object of the type per event), or of the `through` table

through.description: A table with one row per event and object, for events about several objects of the type

event.description: The `through` table's column holding the event's `id` (given with `through`)

clean.description: Clean-up, in this order: a row without a timestamp or an activity is dropped; `where`; `rename`; `drop`; an event about no object is dropped; `duplicates`. Every dropped row is counted by its reason in the build's run

rename.description: Activity name as the data has it to the name to use

where.description: Row filters on the sources' columns; all must hold

column.description: A column of a source table: `table.column`, or a bare name for every source that has that column

duplicates.description: Events of one source that are the same in every column: keep them all (default) or keep one. In a source that names an `id` such rows share that id and an event's id is its own, so the build refuses them: use `drop` there

reference.description: The allowed behaviour, for a conformance check. Its `end` decides when a case has ended (process_performance); nothing reads the rest yet

start.description: Activities a case may start with

end.description: Activities a case may end with

flows.description: Allowed pairs: one activity directly followed by another

any_order.description: Sets of steps that may come in any order

repeat.description: How often a step may happen in one case (default once)

refresh_minutes.description: How often open cases' ages are to be refreshed: kept in the file, nothing reads it yet

examples.name: Supply
examples.description: From a café's purchase order to the paid invoice.
